title: New York picks 10 finalists for upstate new nuclear project
summary: The New York Power Authority has picked 10 finalists to support the state’s plans to build a new nuclear power plant in upstate New York that would produce at least 1 GW of new nuclear capacity. The upstate nuclear deployment is one piece of New York’s larger plans to add at least 5 GW of new nuclear capacity. According to the announcement, the request for qualifications (RFQ) the NYPA issued in May generated 21 submissions from interested developers. The NYPA will select a host community, reactor technology, and development partner “in the coming months.” Eight communities have expressed their interest in siting a new nuclear facility.

title: Landowner and Community Communications to the PJM Board Concerning RTEP Projects
Oklo roundup: Groves-1 plans, Centrus contract, Aurora concrete
summary: Over the past week, reactor developer Oklo has informed the public of several developments through a string of press releases, social media posts, and its third quarter financial results presentation. Most interesting among these was an announcement that the company’s Groves-1 reactor has received Department of Energy approval to transition from its initial demonstration status to an “operating platform for research, testing, and training.”

title: Newcleo And Curio Announce Collaboration To Advance Recycled Nuclear Fuel Supply
summary: France-based advanced nuclear technology company Newcleo and Curio Legacy Ventures, a Washington-based company developing its patented NuCycle used nuclear fuel recycling process, announced an agreement to collaborate on the supply of recycled used nuclear fuel and transuranic materials for the production of mixed-oxide (MOX) fuel at Newcleo’s planned US fuel manufacturing facility. The fuel would be used in Newcleo’s lead-cooled fast reactors (LFRs) once they are deployed. A statement said that by combining Curio’s advanced nuclear fuel recycling technology with Newcleo’s MOX fuel fabrication capabilities and LFRs, the companies aim to maximise the reuse of nuclear materials, reduce reliance on fresh uranium resources and minimise long-lived radioactive waste.
